title: Codify regional networking blueprints and centralize provider pinning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need to reduce ongoing operational friction and deployment drift by (1) extracting a set of canonical, region-aware networking blueprints (VPC/subnets/route tables/NAT/IGW) as composable Terraform modules and (2) centralizing AWS provider pinning and version management behind a single module that all workspaces consume. The current state has multiple copies of near-duplicate networking templates across workspaces, inconsistent provider constraints, and ad-hoc overrides that block provider upgrades and introduce subtle drift during cross-region changes.

Goals:
- Introduce a small set of opinionated "networking-blueprint" modules that capture common patterns (public+private subnets, shared NATs, cross-account peering scaffolding).
- Create a provider-management module that exposes a single source-of-truth for provider versions, region mappings, and default endpoints (to ease upgrades to newer providers such as 5.x).
- Migrate 3 pilot workspaces (stage-us-west-2, prod-eu-west-1, dedicated-ap-southeast-1) onto the blueprints and provider module with zero-downtime and clear rollback paths.
- Add automated CI checks that validate workspace Terraform plan drift and run the new modules in a sandbox before applying.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting application-level infra (autoscaling, EKS) as part of this ticket. That will be a follow-up once networking and provider hygiene are stabilized.

Acceptance criteria:
1) The three pilot workspaces use the new modules and have identical logical networking outputs as before (no IP conflicts, route changes only when intended).
2) Provider versions are defined only in the provider-management module; individual workspaces must not pin providers directly.
3) CI pipeline includes a terraform plan-based check that prevents merging if the plan would destroy existing production resources without manual approval.
4) A runbook describing migration steps, verification queries, and rollback instructions is added to the Infra Confluence space.

Migration approach (high level):
- Phase A: Implement modules in a new mono-repo path terraform/modules/networking and terraform/modules/provider-manager. Include examples and READMEs.
- Phase B: Add a feature flag in each pilot workspace to switch to the module via a new variable (module_enabled = true). Deploy in dry-run mode and run a plan-only CI.
- Phase C: Apply module in canary account (stage-us-west-2) during off-peak; validate connectivity (internal integration tests + kube node reachability if applicable).
- Phase D: Promote to prod-eu-west-1 and dedicated-ap-southeast-1 with the same canary checks.
- Phase E: Enforce provider pinning via a pre-commit hook and CI lint; begin incremental provider updates (minor -> major) in separate follow-up tickets.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: accidental route table replacement leading to traffic blackhole. Mitigation: plan-only gating + manual approval for any plan that changes route tables or replaces IGWs/NATs.
- Risk: cross-account peering dependencies during migration. Mitigation: create temporary peering anchors and sequence migration to avoid tearing down existing peering before the new one is established.
- Risk: provider upgrade introduces behavior change in resource lifecycle. Mitigation: test upstream provider upgrade in a sandbox workspace, and run the full infra integration test suite before merging.

Telemetry and verification:
- Add temporary CloudWatch dashboards (or Console snapshots) to monitor VPC flow logs for the canary namespaces.
- Record terraform plan diffs as artifacts in CI and link them from the ticket.

Docs/runbook to produce:
- README for each module with inputs/outputs and example usage.
- Migration runbook with step-by-step commands, verification queries (AWS CLI snippets), and rollback commands.

Notes:
- This ticket intentionally does not attempt to change tagging conventions; that will come in a separate ticket after the module shape is finalized.
- Coordination required with SRE on maintenance windows for prod-eu-west-1 and with Platform Security for the provider pinning review.

2025-02-22 - Priya Menon (SRE): Reviewed peering approach. Recommended creating ephemeral peering anchors and verifying route propagation before switching traffic. Added checklist to runbook draft.

This PR centralizes provider constraints and exposes a variable to map region -> endpoint override. CI currently failing on provider 5.x acceptance tests; running a sandbox run to isolate issues.

2025-03-03 - Diego Ramirez: Manual verification checklist created. Added pre-merge gate to block any plan that contains resource replacements on aws_route_table, aws_internet_gateway, aws_nat_gateway without explicit label 'dangerous-change'.
